_doc: Registry-only entries linked to their journal publications (read by harness/registry_publications.py): the publication is a REPORT of the registration, never a second trial. Per-outcome states carry held witnesses.

noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke.label: Weitz 2010 (Thromb Haemost)

record_witness.span: 1,146 patients with AF and risk of stroke were randomised to edoxaban 30 mg qd, 30 mg bid, 60 mg qd, or 60 mg bid or warfarin

noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke.identity_check: registry actual enrolment 1146 = publication 1,146 randomised; four fixed-dose regimens + warfarin; 12 weeks (both)

Stroke or systemic embolism.statement: the held abstract reports bleeding and hepatic safety only; stroke/SE is not in it and the full text (Thromb Haemost) is not open -- an abstract's silence is not absence

Major bleeding.statement: the held abstract gives major PLUS clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.2% warfarin; 10.6%, 7.8%, 3.8%, 3.0% by regimen), not major bleeding alone; the full text is not open

noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke.label: Chung 2011 (Thromb Haemost)

record_witness.span: a total of 235 patients from four Asian countries were randomly assigned to edoxaban 30 mg qd, 60 mg qd or warfarin

noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke.identity_check: publication 235 randomised vs registry actual enrolment 234 (one-patient discrepancy, recorded, not resolved); edoxaban 30 / 60 mg qd vs warfarin; three months

Stroke or systemic embolism.zero_events_span: No thromboembolic events occurred in any treatment group.
Stroke or systemic embolism.zero_events_scope: every arm (edoxaban 30 mg, 60 mg and warfarin)

witness.span: No thromboembolic events occurred in any treatment group.

Major bleeding.statement: the held abstract gives ALL bleeding (major, clinically relevant non-major and minor) only; the full text is not open

noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke.label: Yamashita 2012 (Circ J)
noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke.coverage: FULL_TEXT_LOCAL (J-STAGE PDF, read locally; excerpt committed)

record_witness.span: A total of 536 NVAF patients (CHADS2 ≥1) were randomized to receive double-blinded edoxaban 30, 45, or 60 mg QD or open-label warfarin

noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke.identity_check: registry actual enrolment 536 = publication 536 randomised; edoxaban 30 / 45 / 60 mg qd vs warfarin; 12 weeks

Stroke or systemic embolism.zero_events_span: There was only 1 thromboem - bolic event in the edoxaban 45-mg group.
Stroke or systemic embolism.zero_events_scope: the compared arms (edoxaban 60 mg, the approved dose, and warfarin); the one event was in the 45 mg arm, which is not compared

witness.span: There was only 1 thromboem - bolic event in the edoxaban 45-mg group.
Table 2. Incidence of Bleeding Events During the Treatment Period Warfarin (n=125) Edoxaban 30 mg QD (n=130) 45 mg QD (n=134) 60 mg QD (n=130) Major bleeding n (%) 0 (0.0) 0 (0.0) 3 (2.2) 2 (1.5)

Major bleeding.not_admitted_because: a 12-week phase II dose-ranging trial; 60 mg (the approved dose) vs warfarin, 2/130 vs 0/125 (Table 2, treated patients). Admitting it is a served change and waits for Mahmood's decision on the phase II edoxaban trials
